briefs.headline: Tottenham's Williams-Barnett, 18, signs a new long-term contract after his first start
briefs.summary: Tottenham said Tuesday that Luca Williams-Barnett, 18, has signed a new long-term contract, per ESPN; the club did not disclose its length. He scored and set up Dominic Solanke's goal in Saturday's win over Ipswich in his first Premier League start, which made him the club's youngest league scorer since Gareth Bale in 2007, and he has five senior appearances. "This is a special moment for me and my family, and one I have worked really hard to reach. But this is only the start," Williams-Barnett said in a club statement. Spurs, 10th on 15 points, play at Sunderland on Sunday at 9:05 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Marshall women beat Davis & Elkins 80-46 behind 14 3-pointers and 14 steals
briefs.summary: Marshall's women defeated Davis & Elkins 80-46 at Cam Henderson Center on Tuesday before 1,206, per ESPN's box score. Emily Bratton scored 15 points on 3-of-6 shooting from 3-point range, Ni'Kiah Chesterfield had 13 and Olivia Olson made three 3-pointers for 10; the Herd went 14 of 38 from deep, outrebounded the Senators 48-34, had 14 steals and turned 19 turnovers into 27 points. Marshall led 40-29 at halftime, outscored Davis & Elkins 19-7 in the third quarter and led by as many as 35. Seairra Hughes had 15 points and 15 rebounds for the Senators. The Herd are 6-2 and host Ohio on Monday, Nov. 30, at 6 p.m. ET. The men's team (2-4) hosts Prairie View A&M today at 4 p.m. ET, the football team closes the regular season at UL Monroe on Saturday at 1 p.m. ET, and the men's soccer team hosts Wake Forest in the NCAA round of 16 on Saturday; ESPN's scoreboard now lists a 7:15 p.m. ET kickoff, matching WSAZ.

briefs.headline: New Mexico State falls to Ohio 69-68 on Paveletzke's late three-point play
briefs.summary: Ohio defeated New Mexico State 69-68 at The Reef in Jacksonville, Fla., on Tuesday before 146 in the opening round of the Jacksonville Classic, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story. Jackson Paveletzke scored 18 points, 7 of 7 at the line, including a three-point play in the closing seconds; Dusan Makitan had 16, Javan Simmons 12 on 8-of-12 free throws and Siebe Ledegen nine points and nine rebounds. The Bobcats shot 18 of 50 from the field but 26 of 33 at the line to the Aggies' 10 of 13, led 33-31 at halftime and by as many as 11, and never trailed by more than two. D.J. Dudley scored 20 for New Mexico State (1-6), which has lost six straight. Ohio is 4-1 and plays Rice (5-2), a 68-67 winner over UIC, today at 11 a.m. ET at The Reef. The football team hosts Toledo on Friday at noon ET.

briefs.headline: Florida falls to No. 22 West Virginia 70-62 at the Battle 4 Atlantis
briefs.summary: No. 22 West Virginia defeated Florida 70-62 at Imperial Arena on Paradise Island, Bahamas, on Tuesday before 289 in the Battle 4 Atlantis, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story. Zahirah Walton scored 18 points, Gia Cooke had 13 points, nine assists and six rebounds, Khyala Ngodu 12 points and six steals and Divine Tumba 10. The Mountaineers led 37-26 at halftime and 53-49 after three quarters, after a 10-0 Florida run, then held the Gators to 6-of-20 shooting in the fourth and made 7 of 8 free throws; they turned 17 Florida turnovers into 20 points, and the teams combined to shoot 5 of 32 from 3-point range. Kiyomi McMiller scored 18 for Florida (4-3), and Jade Weathersby and Vivian Iwuchukwu each had 16 points and 12 rebounds. West Virginia is 6-0 and plays Notre Dame on Thursday at 11:30 a.m. ET on ESPN2. The football team plays at Utah on Friday at 9 p.m. ET and the men's basketball team plays North Carolina in Charlotte on Friday at 7 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: JSA names three juryo promotions for January and lists four retirements; Hatsu is 46 days out
briefs.summary: The Japan Sumo Association announced Wednesday in Tokyo, after the banzuke (rankings) committee met following the November tournament, that three wrestlers will be ranked in juryo (the second division, the lowest salaried rank) for the January tournament: Oikari of Isenoumi stable, from Kyoto, who takes the new ring name after fighting as Ikarigata; Gojinyu of Takekuma stable, from Hyogo; and Mudoho of Otake stable, from Tokyo, who returns to the division, per the JSA's new-juryo page. The same day the association listed four retirements from the November tournament, all from the sandanme and jonidan ranks below the salaried divisions, on its retired-wrestler page. The JSA's English pages carried no promotion to ozeki (champion, the second-highest rank) or yokozuna (grand champion) this morning. The Hatsu basho (New Year tournament) opens Sunday, Jan. 10, at Ryogoku Kokugikan in Tokyo, 46 days from today, per the JSA schedule this paper read Monday; the full January banzuke is published later in December, and tickets go on sale Dec. 5.

briefs.headline: Flagg's 24 points and 12 assists lead the Mavericks past the Nuggets 120 to 101 in Denver
briefs.summary: Dallas won 120 to 101 at Denver on Tuesday night before 20,023 in NBA Cup group play, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story, Cooper Flagg scoring 24 points with a career-high-tying 12 assists and P.J. Washington Jr. 14 off the bench; the Mavericks closed the first half with 15 unanswered points for a 58 to 39 lead, outscored Denver 68 to 38 in the paint and 35 to 7 on the break, and won a fourth straight. Nikola Jokic had 18 points and 11 rebounds and Jamal Murray 20 as the Nuggets' three-game winning streak ended; Denver and Dallas are each four games behind the Spurs and Lakers in the West. Boston beat Washington 131 to 116 behind Jayson Tatum's 41 points, 28 in a first half the Celtics led 80 to 49, to end a four-game skid before visiting San Antonio on Sunday, and Detroit, without Cade Cunningham, beat Orlando 104 to 86 on Isaiah Joe's 21 points. The Spurs play at Portland tonight at 10 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: No. 19 BYU falls to Ole Miss 73-63 in Maui after leading by 18
briefs.summary: Mississippi defeated No. 19 BYU 73-63 in a Maui Invitational semifinal at the Lahaina Civic Center on Tuesday before 2,400, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story. Adam Clark scored 20 and Corey Stephenson 18 for the Rebels (6-0), who trailed 40-22 with 2:32 left in the half, scored the first 17 points of the second half as part of a 21-0 run and held BYU to 5-of-25 shooting after halftime; the Cougars (6-1) committed a season-worst 23 turnovers against 18 Ole Miss steals and went 4 of 28 from 3-point range despite Collin Chandler's career-high 34 points. No. 8 Arizona beat Providence 84-66 in the other semifinal and meets Ole Miss in Wednesday's final. In Las Vegas, No. 22 Gonzaga routed Kansas State 101 to 61, No. 13 St. John's beat Oregon 90-79, Louisville beat No. 5 Texas Tech 72-64, Tennessee beat Maryland 72-64 and Baylor beat No. 15 Alabama 68-63 in the Players Era 16 first round.

briefs.headline: Ohio State falls to No. 14 Vanderbilt 72-66 on Tanner's late jumper
briefs.summary: No. 14 Vanderbilt defeated Ohio State 72-66 at the Schottenstein Center in Columbus on Tuesday night before 10,757, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story. Tyler Tanner scored 20 points, including the go-ahead midrange jumper with 41 seconds left after LJ Smith's 3-pointer had put the Buckeyes up 66-65; Chandler Bing added 12 and Ace Glass 11 for the Commodores (7-0), who shot 51.9% in the second half and held Ohio State to 34.5% after trailing 57-50 with 5:40 to play. Justin Pippen scored a season-high 22 on 5-of-7 3-point shooting and John Mobley Jr. 21 for Ohio State (4-3), which led 31-29 at halftime and has yet to beat a ranked team this season. Vanderbilt hosts Southern on Friday; Ohio State hosts Lipscomb on Sunday.

briefs.headline: Steelers bench Rodgers for Rudolph a day after McCarthy called him the starter
briefs.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers will start Mason Rudolph at quarterback on Friday against Denver and make Aaron Rodgers inactive, the team announced late Tuesday night, a day after coach Mike McCarthy told reporters that "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback," ESPN reported. The benching of Rodgers, who turns 43 on Sunday and has said this is his final season, was a coach's decision, sources told ESPN; Rudolph, a 2018 third-round pick, won all three of his starts in the final three regular-season games of 2023. Pittsburgh has six wins and four losses after Sunday's three-point loss at Philadelphia, level with Cleveland and one game behind Cincinnati in the AFC North. Elsewhere, the Lions said Martha Firestone Ford, the team's principal owner from 2014 to 2020, died Tuesday at 101, and Denver suspended running back J.K. Dobbins for one game for conduct detrimental to the team.

briefs.headline: Earthquakes beat the Dynamo 2-1 in San Jose's first home playoff match
briefs.summary: San Jose defeated Houston 2-1 at PayPal Park on Tuesday night in Game 1 of their best-of-three MLS Cup Playoffs first-round series, the first postseason match at the stadium since it opened in 2015, per the AP report on ESPN. Ronaldo Vieira headed in Timo Werner's corner at the front post in the 11th minute and Eduard Lowen bent a 31-yard free kick under the crossbar in the 24th; Duncan McGuire headed Houston back to 2-1 in the 80th from Mateusz Bogusz's cross, and Agustin Resch was sent off for a second yellow card moments later. Earl Edwards Jr. made three saves for the fourth-seeded Earthquakes, who had 39% of possession and advance to the conference semifinals with a win in Game 2 on Saturday at Shell Energy Stadium in Houston.

prime.limit: 14- to 20-inch total length slot, one fish greater than 26 inches allowed; 3 per day
prime.item: Prime by the reference file's November calendar, and the Nov. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 24 days old, has the sound's bite shifting toward trout as the water cools; the water at Beaufort read 58.8F this morning, down 4.5 degrees on Tuesday's reading. No cold-stun closure is in force: NCDMF's proclamations index, read this morning, carries FF-31-2026, issued June 25, 2026, and effective July 1, 2026, titled spotted seatrout opening and harvest restrictions, as the current trout proclamation, superseding the Feb. 4 cold-stun closure FF-12-2026, and nothing on trout was issued Nov. 20 to 25. The NCDMF table reads spotted seatrout at a 14- to 20-inch total length slot with one fish greater than 26 inches allowed, three per day; recreational trout harvest must be reported to the division under commission rule 15A NCAC 3I .0124. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits table, read this morning at 5:55 a.m. ET Wednesday; the page states the document is effective Nov. 1, 2026, is for general informational purposes and has no legal force.

prime.limit: 18-inch minimum, 27-inch maximum total length; 1 per person per day
prime.item: Prime by the reference file's November calendar, and the Nov. 1 Fisherman's Post report has the piers taking red drum over 32 inches on the north end of the island and smaller reds inside. The NCDMF table reads red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length, one fish per person per day, with note (C), which reads that it is unlawful to possess red drum greater than 27 inches total length and unlawful to gig, spear or gaff them; the harvest must be reported to the division. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits table, read this morning at 5:55 a.m. ET Wednesday; the page states the document is effective Nov. 1, 2026, is for general informational purposes and has no legal force. No red drum proclamation was issued Nov. 20 to 25.

prime.species: Sheepshead, bluefish, Spanish mackerel and king mackerel
prime.limit: Sheepshead 14-inch total length, 5 per day; bluefish no minimum, 5 per day; Spanish mackerel 12-inch fork length, 15 per day; king mackerel 24-inch fork length, 3 per day
prime.item: The NCDMF table reads sheepshead at 14-inch total length, five per day; bluefish no minimum, five, with note (M) reading that the creel is set by proclamation at five per person per day in private recreational fisheries and seven on a for-hire vessel; Spanish mackerel 12-inch fork length, 15; king mackerel 24-inch fork length, three, both under note (H), which defers to the South Atlantic council and the latest proclamation. Note (C) also allows one black drum over 25 inches per person per day. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits table, read this morning at 5:55 a.m. ET Wednesday; the page states the document is effective Nov. 1, 2026, is for general informational purposes and has no legal force.

prime.species: Black sea bass (south of Cape Hatteras)
prime.item: Open on Topsail's side of the cape with no closed period: proclamation FF-10-2026, the 2026 recreational snapper grouper seasons, effective Jan. 1, 2026, reads for black sea bass south of Cape Hatteras that it is unlawful to possess fish less than 13 inches total length or more than seven per person per day, and sets no season for them; the same proclamation closes shallow water grouper, gag included, outside May 1 through Dec. 31, and bars red snapper possession except by separate limited-season proclamation. North of Cape Hatteras the NCDMF table reads 13 inches, 15 per day and a season open May 1 to Dec. 31, 36 days off. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits table, effective Nov. 1, 2026, and proclamation FF-10-2026, both read this morning.

going_out.limit: Flounder, all species: unlawful to possess outside Sept. 1 to 14, 2026. Striped bass, Central Southern Management Area: unlawful to possess
going_out.item: Not closing, closed: proclamation FF-27-2026, issued June 3, 2026, reads that it is unlawful to possess flounder for recreational purposes except from 12:01 a.m. Sept. 1 until 11:59 p.m. Sept. 14, 2026, in internal coastal, joint and Atlantic Ocean waters, and the NCDMF table lists flounder of all species as unlawful to possess; the proclamations issued Nov. 20 (FF-51-2026, flounder, effective Nov. 24) and Nov. 23 (FF-52-2026, spiny dogfish, effective Nov. 25) are commercial and do not touch the recreational closure. The table's striped bass line reads unlawful to possess in the Central Southern Management Area, where Topsail sits, hybrids included, with note (A) covering the closed Albemarle Sound season and the Atlantic Ocean's one-fish, 28- to 31-inch slot, open year-round; tarpon are unlawful to possess. The Marine Fisheries Commission's Nov. 20 meeting adopted a five-fish recreational bag limit for Atlantic bonito that the division says cannot take effect before March 2027. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits table, effective Nov. 1, 2026, proclamations index and Nov. 20 release, all read this morning.

waters.reading: 75.9 cfs, 1.49 feet at 5:15 a.m., falling on flow against 83.8 cfs and steady on stage against 1.54 feet in the fetcher's 24-hour comparison.
waters.working: The gauge at Dyer reads 75.9 cfs and 1.49 feet, the fetcher's 24-hour comparison 83.8 cfs and 1.54 feet, so the river has shed eight cfs on the day, the flow trend reads falling again after Tuesday's steady, and the stage has slipped a nickel of a foot. At 76 cfs and clear in late November it is a long-leader, small-fly problem and a smaller one than Tuesday's: the fish are on the pocket-water lies and the tailouts rather than the seams, and the midday hours fish best once the sun is on the water. The forage the config records is caddis, stoneflies and sculpin, so a size 18 to 20 midge or a small Blue-winged Olive nymph under a soft indicator on a 12-foot leader through the slower pockets and the tailouts is the pattern, a stonefly nymph as the point fly in the deeper plunge pools where the larger fish hold in cold water, and a sculpin pattern swung tight to the undercut banks in the first and last hour of light. Water this thin asks for a longer cast, a finer tippet and an approach from downstream. The fetcher's read is the verdict: prime wading water.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.77 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 24.89 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 24.8 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: This is the upstream bracket, the pool side, 14 miles above the dam. Normal pool with ordinary bank access, down about a tenth of a foot on the fetcher's 24-hour comparison and reading steady, so Tuesday's rise did not hold and the pool is sitting flat. At normal pool the Ohio fishes structure rather than the slack behind it: the wing dams and the riprap are showing rock, and shad are the forage, so a white or shad-pattern swimbait or a lipless crankbait worked down the face of the wing dams and along the riprap is the pattern, slowed down for water that has seen a run of cold nights, with a jig and crawfish trailer, crawfish being the other forage the config records, on the slack side of the lock wall for the fish holding off the current. The pool flat rather than moving, the fish hold at the channel end of each dam where the current is, so the deep end of the structure is the water to cover. The R.C. Byrd tailwater itself is not gauged.
waters.source: USGS 03201500 (Ohio River at Point Pleasant); config.SPORTSMAN_WATERS

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.22 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 26.19 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.2 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: This is the downstream bracket, below the dam, not the tailwater reading, which the Corps publish and this pipeline cannot fetch. Normal pool, up three hundredths of a foot on the fetcher's 24-hour comparison and reading steady, so both gauges that bracket the dam read steady this morning and the river is flat through the reach. Below the dam the pattern is the structure the dam makes: skipjack and shad, the forage the config records, stack in the current below the gates, and a spoon or a heavy jig worked in the churn, or a live skipjack drifted along the current seams off the lock wall, is the hybrid striper and catfish setup; sauger and walleye hold on the bottom at the tail of the same seams in late November and take a jig and minnow or a blade bait fished vertically along the lock wall and the barge cuts. The riprap along the Huntington bank fishes a crawfish-colour jig on the slack side where the bank current breaks.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 2:12 AM at -0.3 ft, high 8:23 AM at 4.7 ft, low 3:17 PM at 0.0 ft, high 8:42 PM at 3.3 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: low 12:35 AM at -0.6 ft, high 7:18 AM at 6.3 ft, low 1:47 PM at -0.3 ft, high 7:36 PM at 4.1 ft. Water 58.8F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:30 a.m. Moon full, 99% illuminated, 15.5 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 8:23 AM and 8:42 PM in the sound.
waters.working: The moon is a day past full this morning, 99% illuminated and 15.5 days old, so these are still spring tides and the table shows it: the sound rises 5.0 feet from the 2:12 AM low at -0.3 to the 8:23 AM high at 4.7, the morning ebb drops 4.7 feet to the 3:17 PM low at 0.0, and the afternoon flood climbs 3.3 feet to the 8:42 PM high; all four events fall inside Wednesday, none spills over. The surf runs ahead of the sound by 65 minutes on the morning high, 90 on the afternoon low and 66 on the evening high, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills, so the ebb at the crew's spot runs six hours and 54 minutes. The water at Beaufort read 58.8F at 5:30 a.m., down 4.5 degrees on Tuesday's 63.3F. Beach conditions: NWS Wilmington has a Coastal Flood Advisory for Coastal Pender from 5 to 10 a.m. Wednesday, one to two feet of inundation above ground level on low-lying roads along the Intracoastal Waterway and the tidal creeks on this morning's high, and a High Surf Advisory for Coastal Pender from 7 a.m. Wednesday to 1 p.m. Thursday for breaking waves of 6 to 9 feet, with dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion; the Coastal Pender zone forecast reads showers with locally heavy rainfall, highs in the mid 60s, northeast winds 20 to 30 mph gusting to 40 and a chance of rain near 100 percent, going east after midnight, then southwest 15 to 25 on Thanksgiving. NWS Newport/Morehead City has upgraded Tuesday's watch to a Coastal Flood Advisory for Coastal Onslow, which includes North Topsail Beach, from 4 a.m. Wednesday to 4 p.m. Thursday for up to 3 feet of inundation, with the worst on Thursday morning's high, plus a High Surf Advisory from 7 p.m. Wednesday to 7 p.m. Thursday, a Wind Advisory for east winds 25 to 30 mph gusting to 50 from 4 p.m. Wednesday to 5 a.m. Thursday, and a Flood Watch for 4 to 6 inches of rain Wednesday afternoon through Thursday morning. The Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry report, a monthly, is dated Nov. 1 and is 24 days old, so it is the month's pattern and not this morning's conditions: East Coast Sports reports the piers taking red drum over 32 inches on the north end of the island, smaller reds and the occasional trout in the sound and the bite shifting toward trout as it cools; Native Son has cooling water moving trout into the creeks and the 5-to-8-foot seams and cut bait the best bet for the reds inside; Speckled Specialist reports live shrimp under a cork in 4 to 16 feet, 4 to 8 the most common, and 3/16-ounce jig heads with a soft plastic for artificials, with black drum to 18 inches and small reds around; Carolina Flats has topwater for locating trout early, deeper holes later, and soft plastics for reds on the oyster and grass banks; Jolly Roger Pier reports scattered speckled trout, Virginia mullet and spot on the bottom at night and bluefish thick early; Surf City Pier has pompano, black drum and croaker on the bottom. Tied to today's table, a sound in the upper 50s and a northeast wind of 20 to 30: the tide is the whole problem and the wind is the second one, the east wind holding the morning high above the table, which is what the flood advisory says. Red drum's window, the last of the fall, runs roughly 12:30 p.m. to the 3:17 low, in the lee of the marsh banks out of the northeast wind, cut menhaden or a finger mullet on a half-ounce head to hold bottom in the current a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges where the draining grass dumps bait, or a soft plastic on the oyster bars as the water leaves them. Trout want the first of the afternoon flood after the 3:17 low in the 4-to-8-foot creek-channel seams and along the ICWW channel edge, a 3/16-ounce jig head and a small soft plastic worked slowly along the bottom in 58-degree water, or a live shrimp under a popping cork over the oyster bars at the creek mouths; the hour before the 8:42 PM high falls after dark and in the rain, and the dock lights on the flood after that are the night trout water if the wind allows. Spot and sea mullet on bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the ICWW channel on the last of the flood, 6 to 8:42 p.m. The surf's 6.3-foot morning high under a High Surf Advisory with 6-to-9-foot breakers is not fishing water today. Flounder are release only.
